title: Mutational Spectra of SARS-CoV-2 orf1ab Polyprotein and Signature Mutations in the USA
author: Shuvam Banerjee
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgesjtee

steps.title: Retrieve Protein Sequences
steps.instruction: Retrieve SARS-CoV-2 protein sequences from the NCBI Virus database.

steps.title: Filter and Refine Sequences
steps.instruction: Refine the retrieved sequences based on length and quality to isolate the orf1ab polyprotein.

substeps.instruction: Refine output with a sequence length of 7100 (from the initial 7050), noting the target orf1ab polyprotein length is 7096.
Eliminate all incomplete sequences or sequences with undetermined residues (marked as X).

steps.title: Categorize Sequences into Groups
steps.instruction: Organize the filtered sequences into geographic groups.

substeps.instruction: Assign sequences from the USA to Group A (including 867 complete sequences from 31 different states).
Assign sequences from Asia to Group B.
Assign sequences from Europe to Group C.

steps.title: Perform Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA)
steps.instruction: Align the sequences using Clustal Omega with specific parameters and a reference sequence.

substeps.instruction: Align multiple sequences for each group (A, B, and C).
Subdivide Group A into 31 subgroups based on regional source.
Conduct MSA for all subgroups using the ancestral Wuhan orf1ab polyprotein sequence (YP_009742608, 7096 residues) as the reference.
Set the gap opening penalty to 12 and the gap extension penalty to 2.

steps.title: Analyze Mutational Spectra
steps.instruction: Identify and quantify mutations across the groups.

substeps.instruction: Screen alignment results to determine exact mutation locations and associated alterations.
Calculate the occurrence of each mutated variant in Groups A, B, and C.
Calculate the proportion of each variant by dividing the occurrence (a) by the total number of sequences in that group (x).

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Determine if mutant variants in the USA are significantly more frequent than in Asia and Europe.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the p-value using Z-score based on the mutant proportion and sample size.
Use a two-tailed p-value with a significance level of 0.05 to identify signature mutations.

steps.title: Model Protein Structures
steps.instruction: Generate and compare structural models of the proteins.

substeps.instruction: Report wild-type structures of associated non-structural proteins using the I-Tasser server.
Generate secondary structures for alterations using the I-Tasser Homology Modelling method.
Superimpose the alteration with the wild type using UCSF Chimera and PyMOL for visualization and comparison.
